motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Chief Legislative Analyst, with the assistance of the Los Angeles Fire Department, the Department of Building and Safety, the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, and any other relevant department, to report on the fol lowing: • The City's current permitting, inspection, and enforcement requirements for rooftop solar installations on commercial and industrial buildings, including rapid shutdown systems and other fire and electrical safety mechanisms required under the California Electrical Code and Los Angeles Municipal Code. • Existing safety mechanism requirements, such as rapid shutdown switches, and how the City tracks and verifies ongoing compliance over the life of a solar installation. tfi- SEP 1 6 2026 • The adequacy of current protocols for de-energizing rooftop solar arrays during a fire, including why panels may remain energized for an extended period after a shutdown switch has been activated, and what additional measures or technologies could reduce risks to firefighters and surrounding communities. • Any gaps in interagency coordination between the Department of Building and Safety, the Los Angeles Fire Department, and other relevant agencies regarding the permitting, inspection, and emergency response for buildings with rooftop solar systems. • Recommendations for any 'changes to City ordinances, permitting procedures, inspection protocols, or interagency practices necessary to strengthen solar panel safety citywide, along with an estimated timeline and cost for implementation. ~~ PRESENTED BY -W--"'--'-""'<....>w"b-"'--=--~+z!i\-~-~ z
title: Citywide Solar Panel Safety / Current Permitting, Inspection, Safety, and Enforcement Requirements / Commercial and Industrial Buildings / Interagency Coordination / Recommendations / Estimated Timeline and Cost Implementation
